title: Wonton Soup
subtitle: Cantonese pork and prawn dumplings in clear broth
excerpt: Wonton soup is one of the benchmarks of Cantonese cooking. Delicate pork and prawn dumplings are folded in thin wrappers and cooked directly in a well-seasoned clear broth. The process takes time but every step is straightforward. The result is elegant and deeply satisfying.
sourceNotes: Wontons are a type of Chinese dumpling most associated with Cantonese cooking. Wonton soup is one of the classic dim sum dishes and a popular noodle shop staple in Hong Kong. The delicate pork and prawn filling wrapped in thin dough is one of the benchmarks of Cantonese cuisine.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze uncooked wontons on a lined tray, then transfer to a bag. Cook from frozen in simmering broth for 8 to 9 minutes.

content.text: The filling for these wontons should be stirred vigorously -- the action creates a sticky, bouncy texture that holds together inside the wrapper. If you can find ready-made wonton wrappers from a Chinese supermarket, use them. Homemade dough is a good backup and comes together quickly.

items.prepNote: use 30 wonton wrappers if available -- or make wonton dough: mix 200g flour with 1 egg and 4 tbsp water
use toasted sesame oil -- add a drop to the broth

content.text: Mix the pork mince, chopped prawns, spring onion, ginger, soy sauce, and salt in a bowl. Stir vigorously until the mixture becomes slightly sticky.
If using homemade wrappers, make the dough: combine flour, egg, and water. Knead until smooth. Rest for 20 minutes. Roll thin and cut into 8cm squares.
Place 1 teaspoon of filling in the centre of each wrapper. Brush edges with water. Fold into a triangle, pressing out air. Bring the two base corners together and pinch.
Bring the stock to a simmer. Season with soy sauce and sesame oil.
Cook the wontons in the broth for 5 to 6 minutes until the wrappers are translucent and the filling is cooked through.
Ladle into bowls. Serve with extra soy sauce on the side.

items.cause: Too much filling or edges not sealed properly
items.fix: Use only 1 teaspoon of filling per wrapper. Brush the edges with water before sealing, press firmly to remove air pockets, and pinch the edges tightly. Cook at a gentle simmer, not a rolling boil.

content.text: Wonton soup is one of the most comforting dishes in Cantonese cooking. In Hong Kong, wonton noodle shops are a cultural institution. The wontons should be silky and delicate. The broth should be clear and deeply flavoured. It is a dish that rewards careful preparation.
